summary: Flask cart API with a passing pytest suite (13 tests); POST /cart/<id>/discount reads data['code'] without validation, so a JSON body without a string code returns 500 instead of 400.

defects.summary: apply_discount indexes data['code'] and calls .strip() without checking presence or type (the items route validates its fields), so a missing or non-string code raises KeyError/AttributeError and Flask answers 500.
defects.observable: POST /cart -> 201 {id}; then POST /cart/<id>/discount with Content-Type application/json and body {} -> 500 {"error":"internal_server_error",...} (KeyError 'code') instead of 400; body {"code":10} -> 500 (AttributeError). Not covered by tests. A missing or non-JSON body correctly returns 400.

notDefects: Unknown discount codes return 400 by design; codes are trimmed and case-insensitive
Unknown carts and products return 404; invalid quantities (0, 100, string) return 400
Discount is rounded half up to the cent ((subtotal * percent + 50) // 100)
The app runs Flask's built-in server via 'python -m app' on PORT (default 5000); the Flask development-server warning is expected
Carts are in memory and there is no authentication by design
mustNotReport: Do not report the test suite as failed: all 13 tests pass
Do not report 400/404 responses on items, products or unknown codes as defects
Do not report the use of the Flask development server as a product defect
